Jim stood in the center of the mat, trembling not from the heat of the room, but from the sheer intensity of the advanced yoga class. He had meant to join the "Gentle Stretching for Beginners" session, but a misread sign on the studio door had led him here, to the "Ascended Lotus & Beyond" workshop.

The instructor, a serene woman named Seraphina who looked like she hadn’t blinked in three years, glided into a pose that defied human anatomy. "Now," she whispered, "we seek the stillness of the mountain. We become the tree. We become the... long-necked grace of the savanna."

Jim, sweating profusely, tried to mimic her. He attempted a complex inversion, his legs shaking violently. As he twisted his torso to reach for his left foot, his body made a decision his brain hadn't authorized. A loud, resonant *toot* echoed through the silent studio.

The class froze. Eyes widened. Seraphina paused mid-breath.

"Ah," Seraphina said, her voice calm but strained. "The body speaks when the mind is silent. Jim, you have released your tension. Now, hold the pose. Breathe into the void."

Jim, terrified to move, held his breath. But holding his breath while in a twisted yoga pose is a recipe for disaster. His stomach gurgled. Then, another sound escaped him, this one a high-pitched squeak.

The student next to him, a man named Dave who was attempting to balance on one hand, lost his focus. Dave wobbled, flailed, and crashed into the yoga block rack. Blocks scattered like dominoes.

"Focus!" Seraphina commanded, though her eye twitched. "Jim, you are the center of the storm. Embrace the chaos. Become the... the animal known for its long neck."

Jim, confused and desperate to please, looked around. He saw a poster of a giraffe on the wall. He tried to stretch his neck as long as possible, craning it upward while still twisted in a pretzel-like pose. His neck strained, his face turned purple, and he let out a grunt that sounded like a deflating balloon.
